verdict.rationale: Smithery's token-scoping feature lets platform engineers issue tokens restricted to specific connections/namespaces (e.g., 'list and call tools on connections in my-app where metadata.userId is user-123 — nothing else'), which functions as a coarse allowlist mechanism, and namespaces further scope API-key access to a workspace. However, the evidence shows scoping is at the connection/namespace level, not explicit per-tool allow/deny lists within a single server. Missing for 10: documented fine-grained per-tool allow/deny configuration, independent/hands-on verification that tool-level restrictions are enforced, and any admin UI or policy examples showing individual tool blocking within an allowed connection.
